name: Potion Belt
description:
The small bandolier that keeps healing out of backpack tetris. inventory.slotted_bag owns storage truth; the belt is a bounded window onto consumable stacks, so drinking here decrements the same stack the bag counts — a belt holding its own copies of items is a dupe bug waiting to ship. It owns only the use verb: pick the slot, check the stack, apply the effect (through combat.status_effects when the potion leaves a buff rather than a flat heal), and report empty when the stack runs dry. It does not decide what a potion does — that is item data — and it does not auto-pick which potion you meant; ambiguity is the player's problem by design.

The belt is a WINDOW: its slots are the first few consumable kinds the bag holds, in the bag's order, and drinking one removes one from inventory.core_inventory's store — the same store the bag counts, which is why the primitive is declared here beside the bag.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: beltSlots
inputs.description: Quick-use slots. Four is a real constraint: health, mana, utility, and one slot the build argues about.

inputs.name: autoRefillFromBag
inputs.description: Whether the next stack of the same potion slides into the slot when one empties. Manual refill is hardcore; auto is the genre default.

inputs.name: useCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Minimum gap between sips. Without it, a full stack is a health bar with extra steps.

inputs.name: effects
inputs.description: What each consumable does, as {itemId: {heal?}} — item data, which the descriptor says this component does not decide, handed in by the request. An item absent from the map is not a potion and never reaches the belt. `heal` is applied to the player's unit through combat.unit_roster's heal.

outputs.name: beltContents
outputs.description: Item id and stack count per slot.

outputs.name: potionsRemaining
outputs.description: Total across all belt slots, for the HUD counter.

outputs.name: effectOf
outputs.description: What drinking a carried kind would do — {heal} — or null for a thing that is not a consumable here. The inventory panel asks.
